subtopics.title: inference
subtopics.teaching: Master inference within Advanced Reading for National English Championship. Establish the underlying rule or algorithm, trace representative cases, analyse edge conditions, and practise transfer to unfamiliar competition problems. Students should justify the method, identify why plausible alternatives fail, and verify the result rather than relying on pattern matching alone.
subtopics.worked_example: Worked example: solve a representative inference challenge step by step, state the governing rule or algorithm, test an edge case, and verify the final result.
subtopics.pitfall: Common pitfall: applying a familiar formula or algorithm without checking constraints, boundary conditions, units, ordering, or whether the chosen method actually matches the problem.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: independently solve an unfamiliar inference problem, explain the method, handle an edge case, reject a plausible wrong approach, and verify the final answer or output.

Students should justify the method, identify why plausible alternatives fail, and verify the result rather than relying on pattern matching alone.
subtopics.worked_example: Worked example: solve a representative information synthesis challenge step by step, state the governing rule or algorithm, test an edge case, and verify the final result.
subtopics.pitfall: Common pitfall: applying a familiar formula or algorithm without checking constraints, boundary conditions, units, ordering, or whether the chosen method actually matches the problem.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: independently solve an unfamiliar information synthesis problem, explain the method, handle an edge case, reject a plausible wrong approach, and verify the final answer or output.
